source: pdfsource/_pages_headskinv8/p1-p4 (AJCC 8 cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma of the head and neck)

categories.description: Primary tumor cannot be assessed
Carcinoma in situ
Tumor smaller than or equal to 2 cm in greatest dimension
Tumor larger than 2 cm, but smaller than or equal to 4 cm in greatest dimension
Tumor larger than 4 cm in maximum dimension, OR minor bone erosion, OR perineural invasion, OR deep invasion
Tumor with gross cortical bone/marrow invasion, skull base invasion and/or skull base foramen invasion (parent for T4a/T4b)
Tumor with gross cortical bone / marrow invasion
Tumor with skull base invasion and/or skull base foramen involvement

notes.deep_invasion: Deep invasion is defined as invasion beyond the subcutaneous fat OR greater than 6 mm (measured from the granular layer of adjacent normal epidermis to the base of the tumor).
notes.perineural: Perineural invasion for T3 classification is defined as tumor cells within the nerve sheath of a nerve lying deeper than the dermis OR measuring 0.1 mm or larger in caliber, OR presenting with clinical or radiographic involvement of named nerves without skull base invasion or transgression.

N.label: Regional Lymph Nodes (cN and pN share this engine's stage table)

categories.description: Regional lymph nodes cannot be assessed
No regional lymph node metastasis
Metastasis in a single ipsilateral lymph node, 3 cm or smaller in greatest dimension and ENE(-)

Metastasis in a single ipsilateral node > 3 cm and ENE+ (cN: any size; pN: > 3 cm), OR > 3 cm and <= 6 cm and ENE-; OR multiple ipsilateral, none > 6 cm and ENE-; OR bilateral / contralateral, none > 6 cm and ENE-
Metastasis in a single ipsilateral node larger than 3 cm but not larger than 6 cm in greatest dimension and ENE(-) [pN also: <= 3 cm ENE+]
Metastasis in multiple ipsilateral nodes, none larger than 6 cm in greatest dimension and ENE(-)
Metastasis in bilateral or contralateral lymph node(s), none larger than 6 cm in greatest dimension and ENE(-)

Metastasis in a lymph node > 6 cm and ENE-; OR a single ipsilateral node > 3 cm and ENE+; OR multiple ipsilateral, contralateral, or bilateral nodes any with ENE+; OR a single contralateral node of any size and ENE+
Metastasis in a lymph node larger than 6 cm in greatest dimension and ENE(-)
Single ipsilateral lymph node > 3 cm and ENE+; OR multiple ipsilateral, contralateral, or bilateral nodes with any ENE+; OR a single contralateral lymph node of any size and ENE+

notes.u_l: A designation of 'U' or 'L' may be used for any N category to indicate metastasis above the lower border of the cricoid (U) or below the lower border of the cricoid (L).
notes.ene_record: Clinical and pathological ENE should be recorded as ENE(-) or ENE(+).

categories.description: No distant metastasis
Distant metastasis
Clinical classification: stage assigned from imaging, biopsy, and clinical exam before any definitive treatment.
Pathological classification: stage assigned from the surgically resected specimen after histologic review.
Classification determined during or after the application of initial multimodal (neoadjuvant) therapy.
No neoadjuvant therapy preceded this assessment.

notes.matching: For cutaneous head/neck SCC AJCC 8, no separate ypTNM stage table is defined; DescY does not affect the stage outcome and is recorded for clinical context only.

categories.description: Recurrent tumor classification, assigned when the tumor is staged after a disease-free interval.
Not a recurrent tumor in this assessment.

notes.matching: For cutaneous head/neck SCC AJCC 8, no rTNM-specific stage table exists; DescR does not affect the stage outcome.

categories.description: Multiple synchronous primary tumors at the same anatomic site.
Single primary tumor.

notes.matching: For cutaneous head/neck SCC AJCC 8, the m suffix is a primary tumor suffix but does not alter the stage outcome in the engine's flat stage table.
